item.title: The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue
item.description:
Voting
The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue
November 13, 202612:00 PM ET
By
Jude Joffe-Block
Election workers process vote-by-mail ballots at the Los Angeles County Ballot Processing Center on Nov. 5.
Mario Tama/Getty Images
hide caption
toggle caption i
Mario Tama/Getty Images
In the weeks before Election Day, the Trump administration escalated its hunt for voter fraud and its pressure on election officials — especially in California — to crack down on illegal voting by non-U.S. citizens.
Now, with Election Day come and gone, election officials and civil rights attorneys are preparing for the administration to continue its search for noncitizens on state voter rolls, as well as what they see as intimidation tactics toward election officials.
"It's clear that there is this drive to try to conjure up facts that just don't exist. I don't think that's going to change," James Williams, county executive for California's Santa Clara County, told NPR. "So we fully are prepared to continue to deal with this."

By

An animal rescuer carries a cat to safety amid severe floods that hit Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, in May 2024. Thousands of people — and animals — were affected in the wake of heavy rainfall and overflowing rivers.
Tuane Fernandes/The Everyday Projects/Everyday Brasil

Editor's note: Today, November 13, is World Kindness Day!
Kind-minded organizations from various countries came up with the idea and announced it on November 13, 1998. (And the date stuck.) The goal is kinda obvious — do something kind!
It doesn't matter if it's a modest action. One of the founding groups is the Small Kindness Movement of Japan. And no kind deed is too small to acknowledge. One year, the Japanese movement gave an award to a cabbie who pulled over to clear trash bags off the road lest they cause an accident. According to a report in the Christian Science Monitor, the cab driver humbly said it was "no big deal."

item.title: Kratom and 7-OH can feel like 'a miracle.' They can also be addictive
item.description:
Kratom and 7-OH can feel like 'a miracle.' They can also be addictive
November 13, 20266:00 AM ET
By
Rachel Carlson
Kratom and related 7-OH products are widely available at gas stations, smoke shops, liquor stores and online. As early as Friday, the federal government could make some of the products illegal.
Mindy Schauer/MediaNewsGroup/Orange County Register via Getty Images
hide caption
toggle caption i
Mindy Schauer/MediaNewsGroup/Orange County Register via Getty Images
Tyler's opioid addiction began in his early 20s, and when he decided he wanted to quit, he used kratom leaf powders to help ease withdrawal symptoms.
Tyler, now 38, told NPR he thinks kratom helped him stop using opioids for a decade.
Tyler asked NPR to use only his first name because of the stigma attached to his history with drug use and addiction.
In early 2025, he saw a new product at a gas station called 7-OH. He hadn't heard of 7-OH, but said the tablets were advertised as "kratom products." He decided to try them, since the kratom powders he'd taken in the past "can be hard on your stomach," he said.

Kratom and 7-OH products are widely available. They're also at the heart of a public health debate.

item.description:

November 13, 20265:27 AM ET
By
Kate Bartlett
U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, right, and his wife Jennifer Rauchet attend a ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on National Veterans Day Observance at Arlington National Cemetery in Arlington, Va., Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026.
Mark Schiefelbein/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Mark Schiefelbein/AP
Coming out of the bruising the Republicans suffered in the midterms, this week was bearing up to be a bad one for Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. Many thought he'd be the first in the administration to be fired for his support of the Iran war, which proved unpopular with voters.
Then a member of his own party called for a vote to impeach him and, in an embarrassing incident that went viral, he also got chastised for poor decorum when visiting the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
Still, he managed to survive the former – except for Thomas Massie, who sponsored the resolution to impeach him, all other Republicans in the House voted against it – and sought to turn the latter into a PR opportunity.
